title: Instrumented Journey: contextual onboarding overlays with performance insights
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Design and validate a lightweight, instrumented onboarding overlay that surfaces runtime performance and cost signals (latency, token-cost delta, cache hits) inline with the Redwood Console first-run flows. The goal is to teach engineers how configuration choices (batching, model variant, cache) affect economics and UX while they complete setup tasks.
background: Current console empty states and tooltips explain features but don't connect UI actions to runtime outcomes. New customers often overprovision model capacity or disable caching because they don't see immediate trade-offs. Product and Research asked for an in-context educational surface that ties configuration knobs to measurable effects using sandbox data.
goals: Reduce first-week misconfigurations that lead to >3x cost variance
Increase user confidence to try Dedicated/Dedicated autoscale by surfacing predictable metrics
Deliver a pattern that is reusable across rollouts, dashboards, and cost cards
scope: Overlay for first-run 'Create Deployment' flow in Console
Three micro-hints: Batching, KV cache, Model Variant impact
Lightweight instrument animation showing estimate delta (cost/latency) based on sample workload
Prototype in Figma + interactive InVision flows for moderated usability sessions
out_of_scope: Backend telemetry collection changes beyond using existing sandbox metrics endpoint
Multi-language localized content (English only for prototype)
Full rollout to Dedicated private control plane (pilot only in hosted sandbox)
acceptance_criteria: Clickable overlay appears during first deployment creation for new workspaces
Users can toggle each hint and see corresponding sample metric delta
Moderator usability tests (n=8 developers) show 80% comprehension of cost/latency trade-offs
Design passes accessibility check (contrast, keyboard focus, screen reader labels)
Engineering provides a lightweight feature flag to gate rollout
decisions: Use inline micro-overlay vs. full guided tour to reduce time-to-task completion
Show sample metrics derived from synthetic workload rather than real customer traffic to avoid data leakage
Keep educational copy at 1–2 lines; link to deeper docs for advanced topics
Defer internationalization and longform tutorials to later cycles
tradeoffs: Cognitive load vs. value: exposing too many metrics may overwhelm — limited to 3 signals
Immediate instrumentation vs. backend effort: chosen to use existing sandbox metrics API to avoid infra delay
Interruption vs. discovery: overlay appears only on first-run and can be snoozed
research_findings: Participants expected cost feedback in the console but did not trust vague estimates
A small interactive example where changing 'batch size' updated an estimated latency bar was repeatedly referenced as 'aha' moment
Non-ML engineers focus more on cost numbers; ML engineers cared more about cache hit visualizations
Participants preferred a dismissible overlay anchored to the primary 'Deploy' button rather than a full-screen modal
